test_title: PYST 37: SSC CGL 2025 - General Knowledge (Held On: 24th_September_2025_Shift_1)
subject: general
question:
Which of the following statements about India's National and Institutional Sports Competitions is/are correct?

1) National Games began in 1924 at Lahore and were renamed from the IX Games in Bombay.

2) SGFI holds nationals only for boys under 17 in contact sports like Wrestling and Kabaddi.

3) Inter-University tournaments use knockout or league formats and allow one team per university.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1 and 3 are Correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Statement 1:** The **National Games** began in **1924 at Lahore** (then in British India) and were later renamed from the **IX Games in Bombay** (Mumbai). This statement is **correct** as the National Games were initially known as the Indian Olympic Games before being renamed in 1940.

• **Statement 2:** The **School Games Federation of India (SGFI)** organizes national-level school sports for boys and girls under various age groups, including under 17. However, it does not restrict itself to boys only or exclusively to contact sports like Wrestling and Kabaddi. This statement is **incorrect**.

• **Statement 3:** Inter-University tournaments in India follow either a **knockout** or **league format**, and they allow **one team per university** to participate. This organizational structure ensures fair competition and representation. This statement is **correct**.

• *Hence, the correct answer is **Only 1 and 3 are Correct**__.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__

• **National Games of India:**

• The **National Games** are a prestigious multi-sport event held periodically in India.

• It was initially called the **Indian Olympic Games** and was modeled after the Olympics.

• The event aims to promote sports culture, identify talent, and provide a platform for athletes to compete at the national level.

• The modern format of the National Games involves participation from states and union territories across various sports.

• **School Games Federation of India (SGFI):**

• SGFI is responsible for organizing sports competitions at the school level in India.

• It conducts tournaments across multiple disciplines and age categories, including under 14, under 17, and under 19.

• Both boys and girls participate in a wide range of sports like athletics, hockey, basketball, kabaddi, and more.

• SGFI aims to promote grassroots-level sports and develop young athletes for national and international competitions.

• **Inter-University Sports Tournaments:**

• The **Association of Indian Universities (AIU)** oversees inter-university sports in India.

• Tournaments are conducted in a knockout or league format to ensure fair play and competitiveness.

• Each university is allowed to send one team per discipline, ensuring equal representation.

• These events serve as a platform for university-level athletes to showcase their skills and secure opportunities for higher-level competitions.

• **Key Objectives of National and Institutional Sports Competitions:**

• To promote sports and physical fitness across all age groups.

• To identify and nurture talent at the grassroots level.

• To provide platforms for athletes to compete and gain exposure.

• To foster a sense of unity and sportsmanship among participants.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Historical Background:**

• The first edition of the Indian Olympic Games was held in **1924 in Lahore**.

• The event was renamed the **National Games** in 1940 to reflect its broader scope.

• **Modern National Games:**

• The event is now organized by the **Indian Olympic Association (IOA)**.

• It features participation from all Indian states, union territories, and sports boards.

• **Role of SGFI:**

• SGFI is recognized by the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports** and works to promote school-level sports.

• Its tournaments are a stepping stone for young athletes aiming to represent India in international sports.

• **Inter-University Sports:**

• AIU ensures the smooth conduct of inter-university sports events.

• These tournaments are a critical part of India's sports ecosystem, bridging the gap between school and professional sports.

</ul
